It is a tall glass building over 20 stories tall. At the top, the logo of Invesco (which looks like a mountain) precedes the word "Invesco" in white type, on both the west and north sides of the building. Of the main building, there is a division in the giant glass wall on the right side of it, then an overhang off of that about half-way up, where an expensive looking terrace seems to be installed. The division on the right does not extend all the way to the top of the building, but instead stops a few stories short to give the building varying height. Additionally, what looks like a second tall glass building of equally impressive size is connected to this main part of the building at an angle. | image_size = | image_caption = Invesco global headquarters, 2026 | type = [[Public company|Public]] | traded_as = {{ubl|{{NYSE|IVZ}}|[[S&P 500]] component}} | ISIN = {{ISIN|sl=n|pl=y|BMG491BT1088}} | founded = {{Start date and age|1978}} | hq_location = [[Atlanta, Georgia]], U.S. | founder = Charles W. Brady | key_people = {{Unbulleted list|[[Rick Wagoner]] ([[chairman]])|Andrew Schlossberg (CEO)}} | industry = [[Investment management]] | products = {{ubl|[[Asset management]]|[[Wealth management]]|[[Alternative investment]] }} | revenue = {{increase}} {{US$|6.377 billion|link=yes}} (2025) | operating_income = {{decrease}} -{{US$|695 million}} (2025) | net_income = {{decrease}} -{{US$|726 million}} (2025) | assets = {{increase}} {{US$|27.094 billion}} (2025) | equity = {{nowrap|{{decrease}} {{US$|12.231 billion}} (2025)}} | aum = {{increase}} {{US$|2.170 trillion}} (2025) | num_employees = 7,499 (2025) | website = {{URL|invesco.com}} | footnotes = {{cite web |url=https://www.sec.gov/ix?doc=/Archives/edgar/data/0000914208/000091420826000079/ivz-20251231.htm |title=Invesco Ltd. 2025 Annual Report (10-K) |publisher=[[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]] |date=February 24, 2026}} }} '''Invesco Ltd.''', organized in [[Bermuda]], with principal executive offices in [[Atlanta, Georgia]], is an [[investment management]] company. The company has clients in 120 countries. As of December 31, 2025, the company had $2.2 trillion in [[assets under management]] including $407 billion in [[Invesco QQQ]]; $630 billion in other [[exchange-traded fund]]s and [[index fund]]s; $311 billion in actively-managed fixed income accounts; $298 billion in actively-managed equities accounts; $130 billion in private credit and real estate investments; $132 billion in Invesco Great Wall, a joint venture in China; $189 billion in Global Liquidity/[[money market fund]]s, and $69 billion in other types of accounts. It had $1.5 trillion invested for retail clients and $0.7 trillion invested for institutional clients. ==History== The company traces its roots to H. Lotery & Co. Ltd., a UK-based advisory firm formed in 1935. In 1978, [[Citizens & Southern National Bank]] sold its money management operations, then named INVESCO, to Charles Brady and eight partners for $230,000.{{Cite news | url=https://www.fnlondon.com/articles/brady-prevails-on-the-frontline-20010312 | title=Brady prevails on the frontline | first=Mike | last=Foster | work=FN London | date=March 12, 2001 | url-access=subscription}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/stories/2007/11/05/daily28.html | title=Invesco moving global HQ to Atlanta | last=Karkaria | first=Urvaksh | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=November 5, 2007 | url-access=subscription}} In November 1986, [[Britannia Arrow]] bought a 45% stake in INVESCO for £47 million. In November 1988, Britannia bought the rest of INVESCO for £75 million.{{Cite news | url=https://www.pionline.com/article/19940725/PRINT/407250732/invesco-s-u-k-business-hit-hard/ | title=Invesco's U.K. business hit hard | last=Chernoff | first=Joel | work=Pensions & Investments | date=July 25, 1994}} Beginning in the late 1980s, efforts to apply INVESCO's more quantitative investment techniques to the UK equities market failed and the company's investments underperformed in the [[early 1990s recession]], resulting in client losses. In August 1995, the company became a [[public company]] via an [[initial public offering]].{{Citation needed|date=July 2026}} From 1996 to 2001, [[A. D. Frazier]] was CEO of the company.{{Cite news | url=https://www.chicagobusiness.com/article/20010304/HOLD/100016025/for-the-record/ | title=For the Record | first=Sarah D. | last=White | work=[[Crain Communications]] | date=March 4, 2001 | url-access=subscription}} In 1997, the company acquired AIM Management Group and changed its name to Amvescap.{{Cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/1996/11/05/business/invesco-to-acquire-aim-for-1.6-billion.html | last=Wyatt | first=Edward | title=Invesco to Acquire AIM for $1.6 Billion | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=November 5, 1996 | issn=0362-4331 | url-access=limited}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB847066391769462500 | title=Britain's Invesco Agrees To Buy AIM for $1.6 Billion | first=Barry | last=Henderson | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=November 4, 1996 | url-access=subscription}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/houston/stories/1996/11/11/newscolumn2.html | title=AIM's merger will put company `10 years ahead' | first=Kenneth R. | last=Pybus | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=November 11, 1996 | url-access=subscription}} In March 1999, the company launched the [[Invesco QQQ]] [[exchange-traded fund]].{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/invesco-qqq-celebrates-20-years-of-curating-innovation-300809560.html | title=Invesco QQQ Celebrates 20 Years of Curating Innovation | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=March 11, 2019}} In 2000, the company acquired Perpetual, a British investment manager. The company had been founded in 1973 by [[Martyn Arbib]], who was its biggest shareholder at the time of the purchase.{{Cite news |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/business/news/arbib-set-to-net-pound-400m-as-perpetual-finally-agrees-to-amvescap-takeover-635686.html |title=Arbib set to net £400m as Perpetual finally agrees to Amvescap | work=[[The Independent]] |date=October 18, 2000}} The British unit took the name Invesco Perpetual.{{Cite news | url=https://citywire.com/new-model-adviser/news/all-change-at-invesco-perpetual/a217524 | title=All change at Invesco Perpetual | first=Sunil | last=Jagtiani | work=[[Citywire]] | date=January 5, 2001}} [[Neil Woodford]], described as Perpetual's "star income manager", continued to be employed by Amvescap/Invesco until 2013.{{Cite news |url=https://citywire.com/funds-insider/news/woodford-raises-record-1-6-billion-for-new-fund/a758799 |title=Woodford raises record £1.6 billion for new fund |last=Lobo |first=Dylan | work=[[Citywire]] |date=June 25, 2014}} In October 2004, the company agreed to a $450 million settlement with the [[State Attorney General]]s of New York and [[Colorado]], and the [[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]] after the company allegedly allowed over 40 individuals and entities to engage in [[market timing]] trading in mutual funds managed by Invesco in exchange for advisory fees.{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2004/09/08/business/08place.html | title=2 Fund Groups to Pay $450 Million to End Inquiry | last=Timmons | first=Heather | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=September 8, 2004 | url-access=limited}}{{Cite press release | url=https://www.sec.gov/news/press/2004-143.htm | title=Invesco Funds Group, Inc., AIM Advisors, Inc., and AIM Distributors, Inc. Simultaneously Settle Charges Relating to Market Timing Abuses in Their Respective Mutual Fund Complexes | publisher=[[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]] | date=October 8, 2004}} In July 2006, the company agreed to acquire [[WL Ross & Co]] for $100 million upfront and potential earn-out payments to bring the purchase price to $375 million.{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB115370100000414926 | title=Amvescap Is to Buy WL Ross & Co. | first=Arden | last=Dale | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=July 24, 2006 | url-access=subscription}} In September 2006, the company acquired Powershares Capital Management, the sponsor of 36 [[exchange-traded fund]]s which added $6.3 billion of assets under management.{{Cite web | url=https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/914208/000095014407003246/g06401e20vf.htm | title=AMVESCAP PLC Form 20-F 2006 Annual Report | publisher=[[United States Securities and Exchange Commission]]}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/amvescap-to-acquire-powershares-capital-management | title=Amvescap to acquire PowerShares Capital Management | first=Kathie | last=O'Donnell | work=[[MarketWatch]] | date=January 23, 2006}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2006-jan-24-fi-wrap24.1-story.html |title=Amvescap to Acquire ETF Firm PowerShares Capital Management | work=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=January 24, 2006}} In May 2007, the company reverted to the Invesco name and moved its domicile to Bermuda.{{cite news | url=https://www.marketwatch.com/story/amvescap-officially-switches-name-to-invesco | title=Amvescap officially switches name to Invesco | last=Coleman | first=Murray | work=[[MarketWatch]] |date=May 24, 2007 | url-access=limited}} In November 2007, Invesco moved its principal office from London to Atlanta. In March 2008, Invesco renamed its U.S. mutual-fund unit Invesco Aim.{{Cite news | url=https://www.chron.com/business/article/Aim-Investments-changes-name-to-Invesco-Aim-1789676.php | title=Aim Investments changes name to Invesco Aim | agency=[[Bloomberg News]] | work=[[Chron.com]] | date=March 31, 2008}} In October 2009, Invesco bought [[Morgan Stanley]]'s Retail Unit, including [[Van Kampen Investments]], for $1.5 billion.{{cite news | url=https://archive.nytimes.com/dealbook.nytimes.com/2009/10/19/invesco-to-buy-morgan-stanley-unit-for-15-billion/ | title=Invesco to Buy Morgan Stanley Unit for $1.5 Billion | work=[[The New York Times]] | date=October 19, 2009}}{{Cite press release | url=https://www.morganstanley.com/press-releases/morgan-stanley-restructures-investment-management-unit-to-focus-on-institutional-client-base_8bcf2019-bcf5-11de-8b3c-2768eefeca81 | title=Morgan Stanley Restructures Investment Management Unit to Focus on Institutional Client Base | publisher=[[Morgan Stanley]] | date=October 19, 2009}} In April 2010, the Invesco Aim unit dropped Aim from its name.{{Cite news | url=https://www.pionline.com/article/20100222/ONLINE/100229987/invesco-takes-aim-from-name/ | title=Invesco takes Aim from name | first=David | last=Hoffman | work=Pensions & Investments | date=February 22, 2010}} In September 2017, Invesco agreed to buy the exchange-traded fund business of [[Guggenheim Partners]] for $1.2 billion in cash.{{Cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/the-price-invesco-is-paying-for-guggenheims-etf-business-1-2-billion-1506636178 | title=The Price Invesco Is Paying for Guggenheim's ETF Business: $1.2 Billion | last=Baer | first=Justin | work=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=September 28, 2017 | url-access=subscription | issn=0099-9660}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.reuters.com/article/world/invesco-agrees-to-buy-guggenheim-investments-etf-business-for-12-billion-idUSKCN1C33EI/ | title=Invesco agrees to buy Guggenheim Investments' ETF business for $1.2 billion | first1=Jennifer | last1=Ablan | first2=Trevor | last2=Hunnicutt | editor-first=Leslie | editor-last=Adler | work=[[Reuters]] | date=September 29, 2017}} In March 2018, the company retired the Perpetual, PowerShares and Trimark brands.{{Cite news | url=https://www.investmentexecutive.com/news/product/invesco-to-rebrand-investment-funds/ | title=Invesco to rebrand investment funds | first=Leah | last=Golob | work=[[Investment Executive]] | date=March 15, 2018}} In June 2018, Invesco acquired Intelliflo, a technology platform for financial advisors.{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/invesco-acquires-intelliflo-the-uks-leading-technology-platform-for-financial-advisors-300660508.html | title=Invesco acquires Intelliflo, the UK's leading technology platform for financial advisors | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=June 6, 2018}} In August 2025, it was sold to affiliates of [[The Carlyle Group]] for up to $200 million.{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/carlyle-to-acquire-intelliflo-from-invesco-302538062.html | title=Carlyle to Acquire intelliflo from Invesco | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=August 26, 2025}} In May 2019, Invesco acquired [[OppenheimerFunds]] from [[Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Company]] for about $5.7 billion in stock.{{Cite press release | url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/invesco-and-massmutual-complete-strategic-combination-of-invesco-and-oppenheimerfunds-300856770.html | title=Invesco and MassMutual complete strategic combination of Invesco and OppenheimerFunds | publisher=[[PR Newswire]] | date=May 24, 2019}}{{Cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/news/2018/10/18/invesco-acquires-oppenheimerfunds-from-massmutual.html | title=Invesco acquires OppenheimerFunds from MassMutual, will have $1.3T assets under management | first=Jessica | last=Saunders | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=October 18, 2018 | url-access=subscription}} In the same month, the company announced a $70 million investment and the creation of 500 jobs, as it relocated its headquarters in Atlanta to [[Midtown Union]].{{Cite press release | url=https://gov.georgia.gov/press-releases/2019-05-30/invesco-expand-atlanta-global-hq-500-jobs-and-70-million-investment | title=Invesco to Expand Atlanta Global HQ with 500 Jobs and $70 Million Investment | publisher=[[Governor of Georgia]] | date=May 30, 2019}}{{cite news | url=https://www.bizjournals.com/atlanta/news/2019/05/30/strategic-deal-could-spur-invesco-hq-search.html | title=Invesco adding hundreds of Atlanta jobs, will move to new Midtown HQ | first=Douglas | last=Sams | work=[[American City Business Journals]] | date=May 30, 2019 | url-access=subscription}}{{Cite news | url=https://apnews.com/general-news-5ec2aca00bd646f181a9d7511e739dff | title=Invesco to expand its global headquarters in Atlanta | work=[[Associated Press]] | date=June 1, 2019}} In June 2026,
